response.justification: Strong, broad senior engineer with genuine geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and some low-latency, high-throughput systems work in D at Sociomantic, plus a strong testing/quality culture. However, the role's primary requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) in commercial or open-source settings — is only weakly met: the sole professional C/C++ exposure was ~6 months at National Instruments in 2014-2015, with no Rust listed, and the last decade has been predominantly TypeScript/Node.js full-stack work. Systems-level D experience is transferable but not equivalent to modern C++ tiling/pipeline work. Worth a screening call if the team is open to a language transition for a strong generalist; otherwise a mismatch on the core technical bar.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS product experience, including an open-source geo-data platform
Low-latency, high-throughput distributed services experience (async I/O, caching, fibers) at Sociomantic
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, test tooling authorship, mentoring and public speaking
concerns: Minimal and dated commercial C++ experience; no Rust at all
Last ~10 years focused on TypeScript/Node web stacks, not systems programming
No evidence of routing/navigation data pipelines or map tiling at production scale
